title: fix(server): budget counters hold their limit per key, count in a registered cache, and keep the in-process fallback bounded
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9DDnuBdW9LnD9CpSuCNuHyX)_

Refs #29053

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：把 #29216 给 plugin-auth 定下的计数规则推广到 server 车道的其余预算计数器：runtime 的入站限流与端点限流（令牌桶）同一个键的更新在进程内串行；runtime、短信每日配额、notify 节点按地址的邮件限额都按同一规则解析 `cache` 服务（值注册、工厂注册都能拿到，内核自带的 degraded 内存替身不算共享缓存）；core 的内存 cache 兜底在写入时清掉已过期的键，不必等再读一次。
- 为什么改：按维护者裁决「A+C 同意」的 C 半，规则是：每个预算计数器在并发请求下守住限额（同一个键的更新进程内串行），注册了共享 cache 时计在其中（ADR-0069 D2），进程内兜底保持有界。
- 风险与回滚：同一个键的更新会排队，不同键互不影响；没有 cache 插件时 runtime 的限流桶改走有界的进程内兜底，并照旧告警一次。跨节点仍没有原子自增（契约在 spec，本 PR 不动）。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts`（`SharedTokenBucketLimiter.consume`）、`packages/runtime/src/security/kernel-cache.ts`、`packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-cache.ts` 的写入清扫。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/security/inbound-rate-limit-concurrency.test.ts src/security/kernel-cache.test.ts src/dispatcher-plugin.rate-limit-cache.integration.test.ts`，预期 3 个测试文件、15 个用例全部通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The rule, for every budget counter in the server lane: **every budget counter holds its limit under concurrent requests (updates to one key are serialised in-process), counts in the registered shared cache when one is registered (ADR-0069 D2), and its in-process fallback stays bounded.** PR #29216 applied it to `@objectstack/plugin-auth`; this applies it to the rest.

- **`@objectstack/runtime` token buckets.** `SharedTokenBucketLimiter.consume` runs its read, refill, spend and write for one key through `serializePerKey` (new, package-local `src/security/per-key-serial.ts`). That covers the server-level inbound limiter (`server.security.rateLimit`) and every declared endpoint `rateLimit`, which share the class. Other keys run concurrently.
- **Cache resolution.** The dispatcher's inbound and endpoint limiters, the daily SMS send quota (`@objectstack/service-sms`) and the `notify` node's per-address email-field limit (`@objectstack/service-automation`) resolve the `cache` service through a package-local `resolveKernelCache` (`src/security/kernel-cache.ts`, `src/kernel-cache.ts`, `src/builtin/kernel-cache.ts`): a value registration and a factory registration both answer; the kernel's own in-memory stand-in, which self-describes `degraded` (ADR-0076 D12), does not, so those counters keep the bounded per-process fallback and its one-shot warning.
- **`@objectstack/core` in-memory cache fallback.** Expired entries are evicted on write once the map reaches a sweep mark (twice the entries left after the previous sweep, at least 1024), so the map holds at most about twice its live entries without a key having to be read again. No live entry (no TTL, or a TTL still running) is evicted; the `ICacheService` contract is unchanged.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/29053-server-budget-counters.md`, patch for `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-sms`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/core`.

**Local copies, by the seat's decision.** `per-key-serial.ts` and `kernel-cache.ts` are copies of the two internal plugin-auth helpers #29216 added (same rule, same code), one per package that needs them. Re-exporting them from plugin-auth's published `./rate-limit-storage` entry would widen that entry, so they stay internal and are not re-exported from any package.

## Why

ADR-0069 D2 promises a budget counted once across nodes when a shared cache is registered, and a counter's limit is only a limit if it holds when requests for one key arrive together. #29216 measured both halves for the auth counters; the server lane's other counters follow the same rule.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit-concurrency.test.ts` (new, 6 cases): concurrent consumes of one key never exceed the budget, in a cache whose calls each cross a macrotask, in the per-process fallback through the middleware, and for a declared endpoint budget; serialisation is per key; a failing update releases the next; nothing is left in flight once the concurrent updates settle.
- `packages/runtime/src/security/kernel-cache.test.ts` (new, 7 cases), against real `ObjectKernel` and `LiteKernel` contexts: factory, value, none, the `degraded` stand-in, a non-store value, and a bucket counted through it lands in the factory-registered cache.
- `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.rate-limit-cache.integration.test.ts` (new, 2 cases), the composed dispatcher on a real `ObjectKernel` over a socket: with a factory-registered cache the caller's bucket lives in it and the budget holds; with only the stand-in, the stand-in stays empty and the budget still holds.
- `packages/services/service-sms/src/sms-daily-quota-cache.test.ts` (new, 2 cases) and `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-email-field-cache.integration.test.ts` (new, 2 cases), on a real `ObjectKernel`: with a factory-registered cache the counter lives in it and the limit holds; with only the stand-in, the stand-in stays empty and the limit still holds.
- `packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-cache-bound.test.ts` (new, 3 cases): the fallback stays bounded after many distinct keys expire unread; live entries survive every sweep; an expired entry still reads as absent.
- **Forced test edits**: none. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the new notify test's data double (written by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write`).
- Each pin goes red with its check removed (eight ablations, each restored to the HEAD blob).

## Acceptance notes

- **Across nodes, unchanged.** `ICacheService` has no atomic increment, so two nodes sharing one cache still read-modify-write against each other. Adding one is a `packages/spec` contract change, outside this lane.
- **What the rule costs.** Updates of one key wait for each other; other keys are unaffected. The fallback cache's sweep costs O(1) per write amortised: on this shared box, one million writes of distinct keys took the same time as before within noise when all stay live, and less when they expire (the map stays small).
- **The stand-in rule** matches #29216's choice: a cache-less `ObjectKernel` deployment's runtime buckets move from the stand-in to the bounded per-process fallback, which is just as process-local, and the "no shared cache" warning now fires there.
